The divergence compounds -- the relic fires on EVERY elite victory, so a run with three elites upgrades the whole deck instead of at most 12 picks with replacement across a shrinking upgradable set, and sts2_rl/conformance/runner.py:618 compares the deck as (id, upgrade_level) pairs, so any parity run that takes War Hammer diverges immediately. guards.what: N3: C#'s hook is AfterCombatVictory; the sim's run-level after_combat_end is dispatched only on a non-fatal combat (run.py:1206-1208), and the port re-checks run.is_dead
guards.rationale: A naming trap worth pinning, because RelicModel.AfterCombatEnd and RelicModel.AfterCombatVictory are DIFFERENT C# hooks (relic/vambrace in this same batch uses the first, which fires on defeat too) and the sim exposes only one run-level method for both. RunState.finish_combat guards its dispatch with `if room_type is not None and not self.is_dead`, so the sim's run-level after_combat_end is in practice an AfterCombatVictory analogue -- the only way a combat ends without victory is the player dying, which sets run.is_dead. war_hammer.py:18 then re-checks `run.is_dead` redundantly. Equivalent observable, so faithful; flagged because a future relic implementing the real AfterCombatEnd through this same method would silently lose its defeat leg. Rule 7: run.py is NOT hashed here.

guards.what: N4 (DORMANT): the ordering of the upgrades against the reward screen, and the flattened AfterCombatVictoryEarly / AfterCombatVictory two-pass dispatch
guards.issue: RE-VERDICTED from faithful to a DORMANT gap by the 2026-07-26 relic fix pass, to match its two siblings under binding rule 3. `Hook.AfterCombatVictory` (Hook.cs:340-351) makes TWO complete passes over the listeners -- every listener's `AfterCombatVictoryEarly` first, then every listener's `AfterCombatVictory`. War Hammer implements the PLAIN pass (WarHammer.cs:19), so in C# its deck upgrades are guaranteed to run after every Early listener; the sim's run-level `after_combat_end` is one flat walk in `RunState.relics` order (sts2_rl/run.py:1206-1208). That is exactly the position relic/sword_of_stone guard G1 occupies -- also a plain-pass AfterCombatVictory implementer, verdicted `gap` and marked 'DORMANT AT THIS SITE' -- and relic/meat_on_the_bone guard G1 is the same mechanism LIVE (at 38/80 the sim heals 44 where the game heals 56, because index-0 Burning Blood gets to heal first). Per the README, 'no ported content triggers this' is a DORMANT GAP, not a faithful, and dormancy describes today's content rather than the divergence's shape (binding rule 1). DORMANT AT THIS SITE, and the argument is unchanged and still good: the only ported AfterCombatVictoryEarly implementer is relic/meat_on_the_bone, whose effect is a heal, and War Hammer neither reads player HP nor is read by it; the sim runs `finish_combat` before `generate_combat_rewards` (sts2_rl/run.py:1206-1208 then :1210-1213) and `rewards.create_reward_cards` builds options from the card POOL, not the deck, so no ordering against another victory listener changes War Hammer's outcome. WHAT MAKES IT LIVE: porting any AfterCombatVictoryEarly listener that reads or rewrites the DECK, at which point the sim would run it after War Hammer's upgrades instead of before. Grade C (bookkeeping -- hook order only, no numeric effect on ported content). Rule 7: sts2_rl/run.py, sts2_rl/rewards.py, src/Core/Hooks/Hook.cs and audit/records/seam/hook_dispatch.json are NOT hashed here.
